THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ADITYA KUMAR  MOHAPATRA  ORDER 11.11.2024 Order No.
02. 1.

This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/Physical Mode).
2.
Heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the records.

3. The Petitioners are apprehending arrest for the alleged commission of offence under Sections 363/366/376(3)/376(2)(n) of the I.P.C. read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act in C.T. Case No.492 of 2024 of the Court of the learned J.M.F.C.-V, Bhubaneswar, arising out of Dhauli P.S. Case No.57 of 2024.
4. On perusal of the record it appears that the present case arises out of a complaint case.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petitioner has not been named as an accused,
however, since the Petitioner No.1 is the sister of the principal accused and the Petitioner No.2 is the brother-in-law of the principal accused.
He further contended that there is no allegation against Petitioner No.1, although there are some allegations against the Petitioner No.2 of helping the principal accused.

5. Learned counsel for the State on the other hand referring to the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. contended that the victim has stated that she got married to the principal accused in Puri and they were staying in the house of the Petitioners.
Learned counsel for the State further referring to the case diary submitted that the Petitioner No.2 assisted the principal accused ) Susama Mohanty vs State Of Odisha .....

6. Considering the aforesaid submissions, further keeping in view the materials on record, on a careful consideration of the statement of the Victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., this Court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the Petitioners, however, it is further observed that, in the event the Petitioner No.1 surrenders and moves for bail before the learned court in seisin over the matter within a period of three weeks from today, she shall be released on bail on such terms and conditions as the learned Magistrate may deem just and proper.
Violation of any other conditions shall entail cancellation of the bail application.

7. So far the Petitioner No.2 is concerned, it is observed that the Petitioner No.2, if so advised, may surrender before the learned court in seisin over the matter, in the aforesaid case within three weeks from today.

In the event the Petitioner No.2 surrenders and moves for bail within the aforesaid period, learned court in seisin over the matter shall do well to consider the aforesaid observations made by this Court and dispose of the bail application of the Petitioner No.2 on the same day on merit in accordance with law.

The case diary be made available to the concerned court to facilitate disposal of the bail application of the Petitioner No.2.
8.
The ABLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
9. Issue urgent certified copy of the order as per Rules.
( A.K Mohapatra ) Judge Anil Location: High Court of Orissa )
